itens.trecho: Every now and then a production comes along that such an absolute gem, it has you lost for words. A Handmaids Tale, is based on the novel by Canadian author Margaret Atwood . I have not yet read the book but if this series is anything to go by, it will, I'm sure, make its way into my collection very soon.

The Handmaid's Tale was an extraordinary series from start to finish; one of those productions that leaves a mark due to its rawness, its impeccable visual style, and its dystopian atmosphere, which is both captivating and terrifying. Its portrayal of the regime of Gilead and women's resistance keeps you on edge season after season.

People are going to look back at the Censorship decade and think that this and Harry Potter are the only two books the cancel culture freaks read... ... and then realize that they were both adapted for the screen. This was good when they made it for HBO in the 1990s when it had an actual plot and was actually pro-Atwood.
